correctness.rationale: PROVED (conditional on cited First Multiplier Theorem, used as black box and explicitly not reproved): (a) Multiplier application verified: p=13 is prime, 13 divides n=13, 13>lambda=12, gcd(13,51)=1 since 51=3*17, so hypotheses of Beth-Jungnickel-Lenz Thm VI.2.5 hold; standard corollary that some translate is 13-fixed is correctly invoked. (b) Orbit lemma proved and recomputed: mod 3, 13=1 order 1; mod 17, 13^2=169=-1 so order 4; CRT gives combined order lcm(1,4)=4, confirmed by pow(13,4,51)=1 and pow(13,2,51)=16. Fixed points solve 12x=0 mod 51 i.e. 4x=0 mod 17, so x=0 mod 17, hence {0,17,34}; no 2-orbits because 13^2x=x gives 15x=0 mod 51 i.e. 17 divides 5x so 17 divides x, already fixed — independently recomputed zero extra points. Partition into 3 singletons + 12 four-orbits verified, each 13-closed, exact table matches DRAFT: {1,4,13,16},{2,8,26,32},{3,12,39,48},{5,14,20,29},{6,24,27,45},{7,10,28,40},{9,15,36,42},{11,23,41,44},{18,21,30,33},{19,25,43,49},{22,31,37,46},{35,38,47,50}. (c) Size lemma s+4t=25 with 0<=s<=3 forces s=1,t=6 since 25 mod 4=1. (d) Normalisation lemma: H={0,17,34} is subgroup, pointwise fixed since 13*17=17 and 13*34=34 mod 51, so 13(D+h)=D+h; shifting unique singleton to 0 preserves fixedness and difference property; computationally verified F0->F17 shift gives 924 distinct blocks disjoint from F0. Hence existence implies witness in F0={0} U 6 of 12 orbits, C(12,6)=924, verified 924. originality.rationale: Bare nonexistence of cyclic (51,25,12) is NOT new and draft honestly disclaims it: Baumert-Gordon k<=150 table already lists it absent via deep non-constructive tests. Claimed novelty is ONLY the explicit multiplier-13 union catalog with per-candidate spectra and minutes-replayable stdlib scripts for this triple, which live retrieval shows is absent from prior art. Targeted arXiv query all:51 AND all:25 AND all:12 AND all:Hadamard returns 0 results, showing no arXiv record for this triple-specific census. Broad arXiv query (470 results) top hit is Baumert-Gordon which supplies no orbit table, no 924 list, no replay script. Crossref broad query returns only general Hadamard works (Song-Golomb 1994, Golomb chapter, etc.) with no triple-specific enumeration in titles/metadata. Inspected sources: (1) Baumert-Gordon arXiv/publisher record eliminates via Gauss-sum/Mann-type tests, not via 924 difference tables; (2) Carella unrefereed global cyclic-Hadamard/Barker claim gives no per-triple backtracking or autocorrelation table; (3) Song-Golomb refereed IEEE TIT paper treats cyclic Hadamard family generally (Gordon-Mills-Welch, multiplier theory) with no 924-union census; (4) Design Theory textbook supplies the black-box multiplier theorem, not the (51,25,12) enumeration. No retrieved source provides the 924 fixed-translate enumeration, failing spectra, or replay scripts. Therefore the certificate artifact is substantively new, not anticipated, and correctly bounded to certificate-not-discovery.

value.rationale: Independently worth finding later as a citable boundary certificate, not a textbook restatement or parameter substitution. Triple (51,25,12) with n=13 is the smallest composite Hadamard case (51=3*17, not prime so not Paley, not twin-prime product, not 2^n-1 Singer) in v=41-73 outside all three known infinite families; it passes elementary counting (600=600) and Bruck-Chowla-Ryser (1=13-12), so elimination requires non-trivial multiplier+computation, giving motivated boundary status for Hadamard-conjecture tables and binary ideal-autocorrelation benchmarks (R=-1). Contribution is a self-contained seconds-replayable (~0.37s) stdlib-only proof plus full failing-spectrum catalog (maxdev histogram, L2, nbad, best/worst witnesses, 2772-set redundancy) reusable for mining contracted w=3,17 restrictions and sequence benchmarks, archived with checksums and cold verifier. It does not trigger rejection gates: not a textbook proof (textbook gives only multiplier theorem, not this triple census), not mere substitution (principled smallest-composite boundary, not arbitrary parameters), not tiny unmotivated gain (complete 0/924 certificate, not epsilon improvement), not unexplained enumeration (forced by proved orbit counting with canonical lex order and dual difference/autocorrelation verification). Honest scoping to cyclic Z_51 and to certificate-not-discovery increases, not decreases, citability.

residual_risks: First Multiplier Theorem cited as black box (Beth-Jungnickel-Lenz Thm VI.2.5), not reproved; risk of mis-citation is low (standard textbook result, hypotheses explicitly checked) but formal correctness inherits trust in that reference.

Computational part trusts deterministic Python integer arithmetic via two agreeing implementations (double-loop counts vs Counter vs intersection counts plus autocorrelation), not a machine-checked proof kernel; joint bug in both paths is unlikely given separate code paths plus H-shift and group-ring consistency checks but not formally excluded.

Scope is cyclic Z_51 only; non-cyclic symmetric (51,25,12) designs are not ruled out (BCR permits them) — draft explicitly states this, so no overclaim, but future readers must not misread as full symmetric-design nonexistence.
Orbit-table transcription risk mitigated by partition/closure checks and SHA-16 checksum 8a7eae3826de5c31, but downstream users should re-run scripts rather than copy tables by hand.
